name.local: 湘南ヘルスイノベーションパーク

strategy.thesis: Japan's first pharmaceutical-initiated science park, opened by Takeda in April 2018 when it opened its in-house research center to outside organizations; provides wet-lab and office space to accelerate drug discovery and health innovation across ~190 resident tenant organizations.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Former Takeda in-house R&D campus opened to external tenants; now run by neutral operator iPark Institute, a joint initiative of IIF, Takeda and Mitsubishi Corporation since 2023.

summary.en: Japan's first pharma-initiated science park (opened by Takeda in 2018 in Fujisawa, Kanagawa), providing lab and office space to roughly 190 bio/health tenant organizations under neutral operator iPark Institute.
summary.local: 武田薬品が2018年に開設した日本初の製薬発サイエンスパーク。神奈川県藤沢市で創薬・ヘルスケア関連企業にラボ・オフィススペースを提供し、現在約190社が入居。

name.local: 一般社団法人LINK-J(ライフサイエンス・イノベーション・ネットワーク・ジャパン)

strategy.thesis: Nonprofit industry association headquartered in Nihonbashi, Tokyo, that builds Japan's life-science startup ecosystem by connecting biopharma companies, academia, hospitals, VCs and government; runs startup acceleration and pitch programs (including LINK-BioBAY TOKYO) and the UNIKORN overseas-expansion program, and provides members shared lab/office space.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Operates a free 'Out of Box' consultation room for researchers pursuing commercialization, and manages shared office/lab and event space in Nihonbashi.

summary.en: Tokyo-based nonprofit network organization (Nihonbashi) that connects biopharma companies, academia, hospitals, VCs and government to build Japan's life-science innovation ecosystem, running startup acceleration programs and shared lab/office facilities.
summary.local: 日本橋を拠点に、製薬企業・大学・病院・VC・行政をつなぎ、日本のライフサイエンス・イノベーション・エコシステムの構築を推進する一般社団法人。アクセラレーションプログラムやシェアラボ・オフィスを運営。

sources.title: LINK-J
sources.quote: LINK-J functions as a collaborative hub supporting life science innovation through ecosystem building and startup development

name.local: リンク・バイオベイ・トウキョウ

strategy.thesis: Startup incubation cluster launched by LINK-J, BioLabs and Mitsui Fudosan after being selected for the Tokyo Metropolitan Government's TIB CATAPULT program; provides modular wet-lab and coworking space for life-science startups at the Global Lifescience Hub (Nihonbashi) and a directly-operated BioLabs Tokyo wet lab in Shinkiba, plus BioLabs' US-market education program.

summary.en: Life-science startup incubation cluster in Tokyo jointly run by LINK-J, BioLabs and Mitsui Fudosan under the Tokyo Metropolitan Government's TIB CATAPULT program, offering modular wet-lab/coworking space and a BioLabs US-expansion education track.
summary.local: LINK-J、BioLabs、三井不動産が共同運営する東京のライフサイエンス系スタートアップ・インキュベーションクラスター。東京都のTIB CATAPULT事業に採択。

strategy.thesis: City of Kobe's biomedical industrial cluster, launched as part of Kobe's post-earthquake reconstruction and operated by the Foundation for Biomedical Research and Innovation at Kobe (FBRI); hosts roughly 370 member companies, universities, research institutes and specialized hospitals working on regenerative medicine (iPS cells), medical devices, pharmaceuticals and preventive healthcare, and runs accelerator programs/pitch events with corporate partners such as Bayer.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Cluster includes access to RIKEN research institutes and the Fugaku supercomputer; hosts Bayer's CoLaborator Kobe incubator on-site.

summary.en: City of Kobe's biomedical industry cluster, operated by FBRI, one of Japan's largest medical-industry clusters with roughly 370 resident companies, universities, research institutes and hospitals spanning regenerative medicine, medical devices and pharma.
summary.local: 神戸市の医療産業都市構想を推進するクラスター。公益財団法人先端医療振興財団(FBRI)が運営し、約370の企業・大学・研究機関・専門病院が再生医療・医療機器・製薬分野で集積。

sources.title: Kobe Biomedical Innovation Cluster
sources.quote: the innovation arm of the City of Kobe to foster innovation and collaboration among its members and affiliates to ensure a thriving biomedical industry

strategy.thesis: Bayer-operated life-science incubation facility inside the Kobe Biomedical Innovation Cluster — Bayer's first Co.Lab site in Asia after Berlin and Cambridge, MA — offering furnished lab and office infrastructure to university-originated research spin-outs and startups, with pathways to collaborate with Bayer R&D. Foreign HQ note: parent Bayer AG is headquartered in Germany; this entry covers Bayer's dedicated Kobe incubation site.

summary.en: Bayer's Kobe incubation facility (opened June 2018), the first Bayer Co.Lab site in Japan, providing fully furnished lab and office space to university-originated biotech startups within the Kobe Biomedical Innovation Cluster.
summary.local: バイエルが神戸医療産業都市内に開設したインキュベーション施設(2018年6月開設)。日本初のBayer Co.Labサイト。

sources.title: Bayer Co.Lab Kobe
sources.quote: Bayer Co.Lab connects early-stage entrepreneurs with world-class expertise, resources, and global networks with strategic locations around the world, in Berlin, Germany; Cambridge, USA; Kobe, Japan; and Shanghai, China.

sources.title: Kobe Biomedical Innovation Cluster
sources.quote: In June 2018, Bayer opened CoLaborator Kobe, a unique incubation facility for supporting university-originated research and startup companies to create new innovations, for the first time in Japan after the United States and Germany.

name.local: ブロックバスタートウキョウ

strategy.thesis: Drug-discovery and medical-venture incubation program commissioned by the Tokyo Metropolitan Government and operated by Beyond Next Ventures since 2018, selecting cohorts of pharma/medtech startup teams for hands-on business development support, executive-candidate matching, grant-funding assistance, and access to Beyond BioLAB TOKYO wet-lab space.

summary.en: Tokyo Metropolitan Government-commissioned accelerator for drug-discovery and medical startups, operated by Beyond Next Ventures since 2018, providing hands-on incubation support and wet-lab access via Beyond BioLAB TOKYO.
summary.local: 東京都からの委託を受け、ビヨンド・ネクスト・ベンチャーズが2018年から運営する創薬・医療系ベンチャーに特化した育成支援プログラム。

name.local: Beyond BioLAB TOKYO(日本橋シェアラボ)

strategy.thesis: Japan's first urban shared wet-lab for biotech startups, operated by seed VC firm Beyond Next Ventures in Nihonbashi, Tokyo; offers shared bench space, P2-level biosafety cell-culture facilities and analytical instruments (fluorescence microscope, plate readers, qPCR), and serves as the physical base for the Blockbuster TOKYO and BRAVE accelerator programs.

summary.en: Shared wet-lab facility in Nihonbashi, Tokyo operated by Beyond Next Ventures (opened 2018), offering biotech startups shared bench space, cell-culture and analytical equipment, and serving as home base for the Blockbuster TOKYO and BRAVE accelerator programs.
summary.local: ビヨンド・ネクスト・ベンチャーズが運営する日本橋のシェア型ウェットラボ(2018年開設)。都心初のシェアラボとして、Blockbuster TOKYOやBRAVEプログラムの拠点となっている。

strategy.thesis: Cluster of three publicly-backed rental-lab incubation buildings in the Saito Life Science Park (Osaka), offering wet-lab space — including animal facilities and investigational-drug manufacturing capability — to bio ventures, coordinated with Osaka Prefecture's Osaka Bio Headquarters subsidy programs for lab-equipment costs.

summary.en: Three publicly-backed rental-lab incubation buildings (Saito Bio-Incubator opened 2004, Bio-Innovation Center opened 2008, and Bio-Hills Center) in Osaka's Saito Life Science Park, providing wet-lab space to biotech ventures under Osaka Prefecture's bio-incubation subsidy program.
summary.local: 大阪府彩都ライフサイエンスパーク内の3つの公設・認定レンタルラボ(彩都バイオインキュベータ:2004年開設、彩都バイオイノベーションセンター:2008年開設、彩都バイオヒルズセンター)。大阪府のバイオインキュベート施設認定制度のもと、バイオベンチャーに実験室を提供。

strategy.thesis: Incubation and research facility within Kawasaki's King Skyfront (Tonomachi) international strategic biotech zone, functioning as a regenerative- and cellular-medicine industrialization hub and hosting the Skyfront Research Campus for genomic/personalized-medicine bioinformatics.

summary.en: Incubation and lab facility at Kawasaki's King Skyfront life-science zone, serving as a regenerative and cellular medicine industrialization hub and hosting the Skyfront Research Campus bioinformatics initiative for personalized medicine.

summary.en: Incubation operator in Tsukuba Science City that runs the Tsukuba Startup Plaza and wet-lab-equipped incubation rooms for bio/chemistry ventures spinning out of Tsukuba's research institutes.
